Summary: 'Today' quick date-filter sends an empty date range
Description: Selecting the Today quick filter on a dashboard card issues the underlying API request with empty from_date/to_date parameters instead of today's date.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Log in and open Dashboard (/home). 2. Open any KPI/card date filter. 3. Select the 'Today' quick filter. 4. Inspect the API request payload.
Expected Result: The API request should carry today's actual date as from_date/to_date and the card should show only today's data.
Actual Result: The request is sent with empty from_date/to_date parameters; the card shows unfiltered (all-time) data instead of today's.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 -- identical POST body with empty from_date/to_date across 3 independent fresh sessions.

Summary: No validation on Configuration Expression (TC-120)
Description: Entering a malformed Configuration Expression does not disable Save Config and shows no inline validation error.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a Unit's Settings > Custom Sensors. 2. Add/Edit a sensor. 3. Enter a malformed Configuration Expression (missing operand/garbled syntax). 4. Observe Save Config button and any inline error.
Expected Result: Save Config should be disabled and a validation error shown for an invalid expression.
Actual Result: Save Config remains enabled and the invalid expression is accepted/submitted with no warning.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 -- Save Config stayed enabled with no inline error across 3 different malformed expressions, each in a fresh session.

Summary: No maxlength or validation on Sensor Configuration Name (TC-106)
Description: The Sensor Configuration Name field has no maxlength attribute and accepts an unbounded string (tested with 300 characters) with no validation error.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a Unit's Settings > Custom Sensors. 2. Add a sensor. 3. Enter a 300+ character Sensor Configuration Name. 4. Save.
Expected Result: The field should enforce a reasonable maxlength with a validation error for excessive length.
Actual Result: An unbounded string is accepted with no validation error; the UI table later truncates long names with '...', producing confusing rows.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 -- no maxlength attribute, full 300-char value accepted with no validation error, 3 fresh sessions.

Summary: Duplicate sensor name: raw SQL error leaks through the API (TC-104)
Description: Saving a sensor with a name that already exists returns an HTTP 500 with a raw, unhandled database error in the response body.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a Unit's Settings > Custom Sensors. 2. Create a sensor config with a name that already exists for that unit. 3. Save. 4. Inspect the API response.
Expected Result: A clean 400/409 validation response with a user-friendly duplicate-name message should be returned.
Actual Result: HTTP 500 from POST .../api/user/config with raw SQLSTATE 23505 unique-constraint error text (table/column names) in the response body.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 -- byte-identical raw SQL 500 body on duplicate sensor name across 3 fresh sessions.

Summary: Intermittent 500 from unit_general/get on a plain settings reload
Description: POST /api/unit_general/get intermittently returns 500 during normal Unit Settings reload/open flows, more frequently under concurrent access to the same unit.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Unit Settings for a unit. 2. Reload/reopen the General tab repeatedly, optionally from multiple sessions concurrently. 3. Monitor network responses.
Expected Result: The General tab should reliably load live data with no server errors.
Actual Result: Intermittent HTTP 500 {'message':'Server Error'} from unit_general/get (and related unit-get-profile/unit-get-service endpoints); UI does not surface the failure.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): NOT REPRODUCED this pass (0/3) -- 3 fresh sessions x 5 sequential Unit Settings reloads (15 cycles total) all returned HTTP 200. Consistent with the bug's own documented intermittent/concurrency-dependent nature (a plain sequential-reload flow doesn't recreate the concurrent-access condition originally implicated) -- not reproducing under this test shape does not invalidate the original finding; kept as documented, not withdrawn.

Summary: Playback From/To Date: entered value is silently transposed (day/month swapped)
Description: From/To Date fields display DD/MM/YYYY but any entered value is parsed as MM/DD/YYYY, silently swapping day and month for day<=12. Also confirmed in Reports' Start/End Date fields.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Tracking > Playback (or Reports standard report). 2. Enter a date with day <=12, e.g. 03/09/2026 intending 3 September. 3. Observe the redisplayed value.
Expected Result: The entered date should be interpreted and redisplayed as DD/MM/YYYY, i.e. 3 September stays 03/09/2026.
Actual Result: The value is silently reinterpreted as MM/DD (9 March) and redisplayed as 09/03/2026, with no warning.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 on both Tracking Playback's From Date and Reports' Start Date fields.

Summary: 'Playback View' preset doesn't reliably return to the Playback tab
Description: After playback data has loaded and the panel is collapsed then reopened via 'Playback View', the panel shows the Live Tracking tab instead of Playback, despite playback controls still being visible on the map.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Load playback data for a unit. 2. Collapse the bottom panel (Map Focus). 3. Reopen it via the 'Playback View' preset button. 4. Observe which tab is shown.
Expected Result: The panel should reopen on the Playback tab, consistent with the button's own label.
Actual Result: The panel reopens on the Live Tracking tab instead, while playback player controls remain visible above it.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: Names are not unique-constrained across Settings entities
Description: Creating a second Location Control or Vehicle Group record with a name identical to an existing one succeeds with no validation error, confirmed on both entities.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Location Control (or Vehicle Group). 2. Create a record using a name that already exists. 3. Save.
Expected Result: The system should reject or warn about the duplicate name.
Actual Result: The duplicate record is created successfully with no warning; two rows share the same name with nothing to distinguish them.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 on both Location Control and Vehicle Group.

Summary: Assign Unit dialog: 'Assign Units' button never enables (feature unusable)
Description: In the 'Assign units to location' dialog, selecting vehicles registers at the option level but the dialog's own selected-count badge stays at '0 selected', keeping Assign Units permanently disabled.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Location Control. 2. Open 'Assign units to location' for any location. 3. Select one or more vehicles from the multi-select. 4. Observe the selected-count badge and the Assign Units button.
Expected Result: The counter should reflect the real selection and Assign Units should enable once at least one vehicle is selected.
Actual Result: The counter stays at '0 selected' regardless of selection and Assign Units remains permanently disabled -- the feature cannot be used via the UI.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: POI Alert creation fails server-side despite a fully valid form
Description: Creating a POI Alert with a valid unit, POI, and notification channel selected (Angular form reports fully valid, Create Alert enabled) fails server-side with 'Missing required fields'.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Alert > POI Alert. 2. Select a unit, a POI, and a notification channel. 3. Click Create Alert.
Expected Result: The alert should be created successfully given a fully valid form.
Actual Result: An error toast 'Missing required fields' appears and the dialog stays open, with no indication of which field is actually missing.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: BMS Alert and Vehicle Odometer Alert: list never shows a newly created record
Description: Creating a BMS Alert or Vehicle Odometer Alert shows a success toast and closes the dialog, but the list still reads 'No alerts found' even after a full page reload.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Alert > BMS Alert (or Vehicle Odometer Alert). 2. Create a new alert configuration. 3. Observe the success toast. 4. Reload the page and check the list.
Expected Result: The newly created alert should appear in the list.
Actual Result: A success toast appears but the list still shows 'No BMS alerts found' / 'No vehicle odometer alerts found', even after a full reload.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 for both BMS Alert and Vehicle Odometer Alert.

Summary: Leaving the Create Route page redirects to Dashboard instead of Route Management
Description: Clicking Save Route (or Cancel on the Custom Route sub-tab) navigates to /home (Dashboard) instead of back to /settings/route.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Route Management > Create Route. 2. Fill in a valid route and click Save Route (or Cancel with no changes). 3. Observe the resulting page.
Expected Result: The app should return to Route Management (/settings/route) after Save or Cancel.
Actual Result: The app navigates to /home (the main Dashboard) instead, in both the Save and Cancel cases.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 for both Save Route and Cancel.

Summary: Route Name is not actually enforced as mandatory
Description: Leaving Route Name blank while saving a route (with valid origin/destination) succeeds; the app silently defaults the name to 'My Route' instead of rejecting the submission.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Route Management > Create Route. 2. Fill valid origin/destination but leave Route Name blank. 3. Save.
Expected Result: The form should reject the submission and require a route name, per the form's own 'mandatory' hint text.
Actual Result: The route saves successfully with the name silently defaulted to 'My Route', contradicting the documented mandatory requirement.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: Driver create form: Address field is silently required
Description: The Create Driver button stays disabled until Address is filled, but Address has no visible required-field asterisk, unlike Name/Mobile/Email/DOB/DL.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Driver > Create Driver. 2. Fill only the visibly-marked required fields (those with an asterisk), leaving Address blank. 3. Observe the Create button.
Expected Result: Every field required for the button to enable should be visibly marked as required, or the button should enable without it.
Actual Result: Create Driver stays disabled until Address is filled, with no visible indication that Address is required.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: Driver create form: Address field visually appears empty after typing
Description: The multi-line Address textbox's visible viewport scrolls to show the last line after typing, making the field look empty when only one line was entered.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Driver > Create Driver. 2. Type a short, single-line address into the Address field. 3. Observe the field's visible contents.
Expected Result: The field should visibly show the entered text.
Actual Result: The typed text is present in the DOM but the field's visible viewport shows blank space, appearing empty.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 -- and more severe than originally described: the typed text rendered fully invisible in the textarea, not just the lines past the first.

Summary: Driver list export downloads a file misnamed 'Unit_List'
Description: Exporting the Driver list to CSV produces correct driver data inside the file, but the downloaded filename reads Unit_List_(date).csv.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Driver. 2. Use the Export action on the driver list. 3. Check the downloaded filename.
Expected Result: The exported file should be named after the Driver dataset (e.g. Driver_List_(date).csv).
Actual Result: The file contains correct driver data but is named Unit_List_(date).csv, a name belonging to a different module.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: Create Driver: raw SQL truncation error leaks through the API when email is too long
Description: Submitting Create Driver with an email address around 31+ characters returns an HTTP 500 with a raw, unhandled SQL Server truncation error, with no client-side length validation to catch it first.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Settings > Driver > Create Driver. 2. Fill a valid-looking form with an email address 31+ characters long. 3. Submit.
Expected Result: The form should validate email length client-side, or the server should return a clean validation error.
Actual Result: HTTP 500 from POST /api/add-driver with the raw SQLSTATE[42000] truncation error (table/column names) in the response body.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 -- identical SQLSTATE truncation error every time; also observed the same class of bug triggers off an over-length Name value, truncating at the name column instead -- worth noting as a related manifestation, not a separate bug.

Summary: Vehicle Summary, Trip Report and Cumulative Distance fail with a raw SQL error for any date range whose monthly telemetry table doesn't exist
Description: These three reports' queries reference a monthly telemetry partition table directly; when no partition exists for the requested month, the query throws a raw SQL 500 instead of returning zero rows -- reproduces for any month with no data, not one isolated case.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Reports > Standard > Vehicle Summary (or Trip Report / Cumulative Distance). 2. Select a date range in a month with no telemetry data for the account. 3. Generate.
Expected Result: The report should return a clean 'no data' state for a date range with no telemetry.
Actual Result: HTTP 500 with a raw SQLSTATE[42S02] 'Invalid object name' error (referencing the specific missing monthly partition table) in the response body.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 across all three affected report types (Vehicle Summary, Trip Report, Cumulative Distance).

Summary: Fleet Summary KPI cards can display a stale value from an earlier, slower request
Description: The KPI cards are populated from a separate API call with no request-sequencing guard; a slower earlier all-vehicles request can overwrite the cards with stale data after a faster later single-vehicle request has already rendered correctly.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Reports > Standard > Fleet Summary. 2. Generate for all vehicles (slow). 3. Immediately switch to and generate for a single vehicle (fast, resolves first). 4. Wait for the slow request to also resolve.
Expected Result: The KPI cards should reflect the currently-selected filter/report only.
Actual Result: The KPI cards briefly show the correct single-vehicle value, then get overwritten back to the stale all-vehicles value once the slower request resolves.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): NOT REPRODUCED this pass -- the app now blocks the UI action needed to create the interleaving (the Filters/Generate control stays non-interactive until the in-flight slow request resolves), so the described request race could not be triggered via the UI across 6 attempts using 2 different methodologies. Possibly fixed since the original finding, or requires bypassing the UI with raw concurrent API calls to reach -- flagged for follow-up rather than closed outright.

Summary: A failed report-generation request leaves the UI permanently stuck on 'Generating...'
Description: If the report-table API call fails at the network level, the Generate button switches to 'Generating...' and never recovers -- no error, no retry, no timeout handling.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open any Standard Report. 2. Simulate/encounter a network failure during Generate (e.g. connection drop). 3. Observe the Generate button.
Expected Result: The UI should show an error/retry state after a failed request, not remain stuck loading indefinitely.
Actual Result: The button permanently shows 'Generating...' with no error message or retry affordance; the only escape is leaving the report form.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: Fleet Summary with all vehicles selected hangs on 'Generating...' forever, even though both backend calls succeed
Description: Selecting all vehicles via 'Select All' for Fleet Summary and generating never renders a result, despite both underlying API calls returning HTTP 200 -- the frontend never transitions out of the loading state.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Reports > Standard > Fleet Summary. 2. Click 'Select All' to select all vehicles. 3. Click Generate. 4. Wait 45+ seconds.
Expected Result: The report/KPI cards should render using the successfully-returned data.
Actual Result: The Generate button stays permanently on 'Generating...'; the table shows a static loading skeleton with 0 real rows bound, despite both backend calls succeeding.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): NOT REPRODUCED this pass -- an initial false positive (a stale "Generating..." label sitting in a closed, off-screen Filters drawer) was ruled out; on proper re-test, all-vehicles Fleet Summary rendered correctly with real data in 2.3-6.9s across 6 attempts (3 all-vehicles + 3 single-vehicle), no hang, no stuck skeleton rows, no zero pagination. Possibly fixed since the original finding.

Summary: KPI Settings' 'Select All' paradoxically deselects down to the protected minimum when already fully selected
Description: Clicking 'Select All' in Home's KPI Settings while already at full selection (10/10) drops the selection down to the protected minimum (6) instead of staying at 10, with no relabeling of the button.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Home > KPI Settings with all 10 KPIs already selected. 2. Click 'Select All' again. 3. Click Save. 4. Observe the header KPIs.
Expected Result: Clicking 'Select All' while already fully selected should be a no-op (stay at 10 selected).
Actual Result: The selection drops to the protected minimum of 6, silently removing 4 KPIs once Save is clicked.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: Two of a Group's five status chips ('Active' and 'No Data') always filter Fleet to zero vehicles
Description: On Home's Groups tab, clicking the 'Active' or 'No Data' status chip always filters Fleet to 0 vehicles regardless of the group or the chip's own displayed count; Running/Idle/Stopped work correctly.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Home > Groups tab. 2. Click the 'Active (N)' or 'No Data (N)' chip on any group card. 3. Observe the filtered Fleet list.
Expected Result: Clicking a status chip should filter Fleet to the matching vehicles, consistent with the chip's own count.
Actual Result: Fleet always shows 0 vehicles for 'Active' and 'No Data' chips, confirmed across multiple groups and both large and single-vehicle samples.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3, tested across 2 different groups x 2 chips per run (6 combinations total, all 3 runs).

Summary: A 'Map only' GeoLink still exposes the vehicle's identifying registration number to anonymous visitors
Description: Creating a 'Map only' GeoLink (promised as 'vehicle location without details') and opening its public URL in an unauthenticated context shows the vehicle's full registration/identifying string anyway.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Home > GeoLinks. 2. Create a 'Map only' share link for a vehicle. 3. Open the real public URL in a fresh, unauthenticated browser context (no login/cookies). 4. Observe the page content.
Expected Result: A 'Map only' link should show only an anonymous location pin, with no vehicle-identifying details.
Actual Result: The vehicle's full registration/identifying string is shown directly on the page, alongside status and distance -- contradicting the access level's own stated promise.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: Closing the Create User wizard without clicking Submit still permanently creates the user
Description: Step 1 to Step 2 of the Create User wizard makes a real, immediate save API call; closing the wizard at any later point without ever clicking Submit does not roll back the already-created user.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Administrator > Create User. 2. Fill Step 1 and click Next Step. 3. Progress through further steps without configuring menu/permissions if desired. 4. Close the wizard via the 'X' icon instead of clicking Submit. 5. Check User Management.
Expected Result: A user should only be considered created after the final Submit succeeds, per the module's own design intent.
Actual Result: A real, permanent user account is created with default/empty authorization the moment Step 1's Next Step is clicked, regardless of whether the wizard is ever completed or submitted.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: 'Add Group' on the Create User wizard re-fetches its static menu list from the API on every click, with no loading indicator or debounce
Description: Clicking 'Add Group' in Step 2 always re-fetches an effectively static menu list (multi-second unindicated delay) and has no debounce, so rapid clicks stack multiple duplicate dialogs.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Administrator > Create User wizard, Step 2 (Menu Access). 2. Click 'Add Group' once and time the delay before the dialog appears. 3. Click 'Add Group' multiple times rapidly. 4. Count open dialogs.
Expected Result: The menu list should be fetched once and cached/reused; the button should be disabled or debounced while a fetch/dialog-open is in progress.
Actual Result: Every click re-issues the same API call with no loading feedback; rapid clicks stack one independent dialog per click (confirmed 1 -> 4 dialogs after 3 rapid clicks).
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 for the stacking defect; the open-delay is confirmed present every time (1.16-1.29s) though measured smaller than the originally reported ~5s.

Summary: Step 4's unit selector is a separate, unfiltered picker over the entire fleet, disconnected from Step 1's vehicle scope (confirmed harmless, UX-only)
Description: Step 4 (Unit Permission) lists the entire fleet regardless of Step 1's vehicle scope, with no visual indication of which options are actually in scope. Confirmed via a follow-up authorization test that the resulting permission has no real effect outside Step 1's scope.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Administrator > Create User wizard. 2. In Step 1, select only one vehicle. 3. In Step 4, observe the unit selector's full option list.
Expected Result: Step 4's unit list should be filtered to (or visually flag) Step 1's selected vehicle scope.
Actual Result: Step 4 shows the entire fleet (30+ other vehicles never chosen in Step 1) with no visual distinction of in-scope vs out-of-scope options.
Reverification Note: Live page captured; confirmed harmless from a security standpoint via a prior effective-authorization test (Phase 8) -- UX-only finding, not re-triggered this pass.

Summary: [CRITICAL] Clicking 'Edit' on a user row opens a completely different, unrelated user's data
Description: Clicking a specific, searched-down-to-one user row's Edit action opens the Edit dialog pre-bound to a different, unrelated existing username instead of the clicked user, reproduced across independent sessions with a clean-overlay-state check ruling out a stale dialog.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create or identify a specific sub-user in Administrator > User Management. 2. Search down to exactly that one matching row. 3. Click that row's Edit user action. 4. Observe the dialog title/bound user.
Expected Result: The Edit dialog should open bound to the exact user whose row's Edit action was clicked.
Actual Result: The dialog opens titled for a different, unrelated pre-existing username ('Tarunn'), confirmed reproducible across independent sessions with zero pre-existing overlay panes before the click.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3, including the stale-dialog-artifact control (0 overlay panes immediately before the Edit click, exactly 1 immediately after) ruling out the alternate explanation in every attempt.

Summary: Menu Access is only enforced by hiding nav items -- direct URL navigation reaches modules a sub-user was never granted
Description: A sub-user's Menu Access is implemented as client-side nav-item hiding only; navigating a sub-user directly to /settings/driver or /administrator by URL loads the real page shell, including a functional Administrator/User Management page for a sub-user never granted Administrator.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create a sub-user with a menu group granting only Home/Dashboard/Tracking. 2. Log in as that sub-user. 3. Navigate directly to /administrator (or /settings/driver) by URL.
Expected Result: Direct URL navigation to an ungranted module should be blocked/redirected (a real route guard), not just hidden from the nav.
Actual Result: The real page shell loads normally for both URLs; /administrator in particular loads a fully functional User Management page (showing '0 users') for a sub-user who should never be able to reach it under any configuration.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: General Permission category 'User' is relabelled 'Global' between the Create wizard and the Permissions dialog
Description: The Create User wizard's Step 3 General Permission category named 'User' is the same category, on the same account/user, labelled 'Global' when reopened via the row's Permissions action.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Administrator > Create User wizard, Step 3, and note the 'User' General Permission category. 2. For the same user, open the row's Permissions (manage_accounts icon) action's General Permission tab. 3. Compare category labels.
Expected Result: The same permission category should be labelled consistently across both surfaces.
Actual Result: The identical category is labelled 'User' during creation and 'Global' when re-opened via Permissions, for the same user/account.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: Unicode (non-Latin) characters in a username are corrupted to literal '?' characters
Description: Creating a sub-user with a Chinese-character username results in the displayed username becoming literal '?' characters after creation and a page reload -- real character corruption, not a font-rendering issue.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Administrator > Create User. 2. Enter a username containing non-Latin (e.g. Chinese) characters. 3. Complete creation and reload the page. 4. Observe the username in User Management.
Expected Result: The original Unicode username should be preserved and displayed correctly.
Actual Result: The Chinese characters are replaced with literal '?' characters, a classic sign of a text-encoding mismatch somewhere in the save/reload/render pipeline.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: 'User already exists' error for common usernames the account doesn't actually have -- appears globally scoped with a misleading message
Description: Creating sub-users named 'test', 'admin', or 'demo' in an account with no such existing users all fail with 'user already exists' (app's own typo: user_alread_exist), while a more specific name is accepted normally; the underlying save call returns HTTP 200 even for the rejected names.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. In an account with no users named 'test'/'admin'/'demo', open Administrator > Create User. 2. Attempt to create a user named 'test' (then 'admin', then 'demo'). 3. Observe the error and the same-account user list.
Expected Result: Either the check should be scoped per-account, or the error message should clarify the collision is with a username taken elsewhere on the platform.
Actual Result: All three common names are rejected as 'already exists' despite not existing in this account, suggesting a global (not per-account) uniqueness check with a misleading, account-scoped-sounding error message.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3 (9/9 individual attempts across "test"/"admin"/"demo") -- confirmed HTTP 200 with status:false, message:"user_alread_exist" [sic] every time.

Summary: [Low] No show/hide (eye) toggle on the Password / Confirm Password fields in the Create User wizard
Description: Step 1's Password and Confirm Password fields are plain type=password inputs with no visibility-toggle control, inconsistent with the User Management table's own working password-reveal toggle per row.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Administrator > Create User wizard, Step 1. 2. Locate the Password and Confirm Password fields. 3. Look for a visibility-toggle (eye) icon.
Expected Result: A visibility toggle should be available, consistent with the same capability already present in the User Management table.
Actual Result: No visibility toggle exists on either field in the wizard, though the same capability exists elsewhere in the module (User Management's per-row 'Show password').
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: At mobile viewport widths, the Account menu is not reachable through any UI control
Description: At a 390x844 mobile viewport, the desktop Account-menu avatar button becomes invisible and no alternative control opens My Profile, Support, Change Password, Language, or Sign Out.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Set the browser viewport to 390x844 (or a similar phone size). 2. Log in and look for the Account menu (avatar button). 3. Try the hamburger/menu toggle and any other visible control.
Expected Result: A mobile-appropriate control should provide access to My Profile, Support, Change Password, Language, and Sign Out.
Actual Result: The desktop avatar button is invisible; the mobile hamburger only toggles the primary nav list. No control anywhere in the mobile layout opens the Account menu items, including Sign Out.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: [CRITICAL] Raise Support Ticket cannot be submitted -- vehicle counter never updates, and Submit stays permanently disabled on a fully valid form
Description: The 'X selected' vehicle counter in Raise Support Ticket never updates from '0 selected' despite real selections registering at the component level, and the Submit Ticket button never enables even with every field genuinely valid (no visible errors anywhere), verified across four different input methods.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Profile > Support > Raise Ticket. 2. Select one or more vehicles, a Category, a Severity, and enter a valid Comment, Email, and Mobile. 3. Observe the selected-count indicator and the Submit Ticket button.
Expected Result: The selected-count indicator should reflect the real selection, and Submit Ticket should enable once the form is genuinely valid.
Actual Result: The counter stays at '0 selected' regardless of real selection, and Submit Ticket never enables even on a fully valid form -- the ticket cannot be submitted through the UI.
Reverification Note: Reverified 2026-09-07 (live 3x pass): REPRODUCED 3/3.

Summary: [Low] Raise Support Ticket's Comment field ignores any programmatic value change -- only real keystrokes register
Description: The Comment textarea never registers a value set via a standard programmatic value+input-event write; only genuine keystroke-by-keystroke input updates the value, counter, and Angular form state.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Profile > Support > Raise Ticket. 2. Attempt to set the Comment field's value via paste, autofill, or another non-keystroke method. 3. Observe the field's value and the character counter.
